description:
DIAGNOSIS (stands, twice confirmed): analysis settledness is cycle-bound.
Every call edge is a two-evaluator cycle -- caller publishes the callee's
inputs, callee publishes the return, caller reads it -- and only the drain
arbiter discharges those facts. Confirmed structurally during fz-kdt.13.2
(one trace suffices: semantic.rs reads/publishes) and again by fz-kdt.74's
cold review: the cycle is INTERPROCEDURAL RETURN FLOW, not an artifact of
key-level aggregation -- no identity re-plumbing removes it (that claim is
in fz-kdt.74's graveyard).

THE LEVER (gated): waits carry no derivation attribution, so a satisfied
wait dirties every answer a job holds (scheduler enqueue_dependents ->
dirty_job_claims); measured 12-25% of AnalyzeActivation completions block.
Giving waits derivation attribution (or scoping blocks) stops job-wide
re-dirtying -- but it only pays once split answers exist, i.e. once
fz-kdt.13.2 is unparked, and whether THAT pays is decided by fz-kdt.83's
census (if zero-change churn dominates, wake precision -- possibly this very
lever -- is the campaign; if genuine ascent dominates, the widening ladder
is, and this waits).

Sequenced: after fz-kdt.83.
title: The caller-callee return cycle is fundamental; wait attribution is the gated lever
